topic-088-a-cautionary-tale-on-integrati.evolution: The representatives move from therapy-effectiveness and dose-response modeling to heterogeneous effects, proximal methods, and combining environments. Recent work considers budgeted experiments, abstaining from uncertain responder classifications, and diagnosing mechanisms behind observational bias. These are complementary ways to make the limits of available evidence more actionable.
openQuestions: When can additional experiments resolve important ambiguities left by observational data?
How can bias mechanisms be distinguished when multiple sources operate together?
topic-088-a-cautionary-tale-on-integrati.overview: Treatment-effect estimation asks how outcomes would change under an intervention, including how effects vary between individuals. These papers study observational data, randomized evidence, proxy variables, instruments, and partial identification. The missing counterfactual makes this different from ordinary prediction: an accurate outcome model does not by itself establish a valid causal comparison.
topic-088-a-cautionary-tale-on-integrati.title: Treatment Effects under Confounding and Selection Bias
topic-088-a-cautionary-tale-on-integrati.whyItMatters: Decisions about interventions need an account of who receives treatment and why. Explicit assumptions and uncertainty can prevent precise-looking estimates from concealing hidden confounding, selection effects, or differences between study populations.

topic-089-distributed-and-provably-good-.evolution: Early representatives study convergence and improved starting points. Later work adds stable instances, fairness, missing values, and dynamic updates. Recent analyses contrast Lloyd and Hartigan updates in high-dimensional noise, showing that algorithms targeting the same objective can behave very differently.
openQuestions: Which stability measures predict useful clusters in real applications?
Can compact coresets preserve fairness and robustness as well as the clustering objective?
topic-089-distributed-and-provably-good-.overview: Geometric clustering groups points around representative centers, often by minimizing distances as in k-means. This topic examines initialization, local search, approximation guarantees, compressed datasets called coresets, and sensitivity to missing or changing observations. A representative stability analysis measures how much an algorithm's output changes when a random input point is removed.
topic-089-distributed-and-provably-good-.title: Geometric Clustering, Stability, and Coresets
topic-089-distributed-and-provably-good-.whyItMatters: A low clustering objective does not guarantee that the result is stable or that a particular optimizer will find meaningful groups. Algorithmic guarantees clarify the effects of dimension, noise, initialization, and data reduction on practical conclusions.

topic-090-a-causal-framework-for-decompo.evolution: Earlier representatives connect causal parameter estimation with learning rules and non-Gaussian temporal models. Later work expands to nonlinear confounders and causal disentanglement. Recent spatial methods use neighboring treatments as proxies for latent confounding while explicitly accounting for interference, alongside robustness studies of noise and temporal distributions.
openQuestions: Which latent-variable assumptions have observable implications that can be checked?
How sensitive are recovered structures and effects to imperfect proxies or misspecified noise models?
topic-090-a-causal-framework-for-decompo.overview: Causal discovery becomes harder when important variables are unobserved. This topic studies when causal structures or their numerical parameters can still be recovered using distributional assumptions, proxy measurements, temporal information, or special graphical conditions. A representative analysis separates different parameter ambiguities in partially observed linear models and identifies conditions that resolve them.
topic-090-a-causal-framework-for-decompo.title: Latent Confounding and Causal Model Identifiability
topic-090-a-causal-framework-for-decompo.whyItMatters: Hidden variables can make several causal explanations observationally equivalent. Identifiability results show which conclusions follow from the evidence and which depend on assumptions that prediction accuracy alone cannot validate.

topic-091-why-is-there-a-tumor-tell-me-t.evolution: The representatives begin with partially labeled images and structured scene parsing. Later work develops object candidates and general-purpose segmentation. Recent papers explore unsupervised multi-object discovery, language prompts, generative segmentation, and which properties of synthetic images improve dense visual representations.
openQuestions: How can automatically generated masks be checked without recreating a full labeling effort?
Which synthetic scene properties transfer reliably to unfamiliar real-world imagery?
topic-091-why-is-there-a-tumor-tell-me-t.overview: Segmentation assigns pixels to meaningful objects or regions. This cluster focuses on reducing annotation requirements and making segmentation responsive to prompts, language, and broader visual understanding. One unsupervised approach builds hierarchical masks by combining top-down image partitioning with bottom-up merging, then uses those masks to train a promptable segmentation model.
topic-091-why-is-there-a-tumor-tell-me-t.title: Promptable Segmentation and Learning from Weak Visual Supervision
topic-091-why-is-there-a-tumor-tell-me-t.whyItMatters: Dense human labels are expensive and may omit objects outside an annotation scheme. Weak supervision, automatically discovered masks, and synthetic scenes can widen coverage, but their usefulness depends on spatial detail and the quality of object boundaries.

topic-092-pocket2mol-efficient-molecular.evolution: Early representatives predict protein function and drug activity from structured features. Later work develops learned molecular graph generators and data-efficient grammars. Recent papers add multimodal foundation models and synthesis-aware rewards, while retrosynthesis benchmarks question whether matching a single recorded answer fairly evaluates an open-ended chemical problem.
openQuestions: How can generation balance novelty, predicted utility, and synthesizability?
What independent evidence should validate chemical-plausibility metrics used to train and evaluate models?
topic-092-pocket2mol-efficient-molecular.overview: Molecules can be represented as graphs whose atoms and bonds support property prediction, generation, and synthesis planning. These papers investigate graph neural networks, variational generators, molecular grammars, and flow networks. A representative graph autoencoder generates molecules through sequential extension steps and shapes its latent space to favor desired properties.
topic-092-pocket2mol-efficient-molecular.title: Molecular Graph Learning and Chemically Constrained Generation
topic-092-pocket2mol-efficient-molecular.whyItMatters: A graph can satisfy a model's objective while remaining difficult to synthesize or chemically unhelpful. Chemical constraints, interpretable construction rules, and suitable evaluation criteria help connect statistical generation to practical molecular design.

topic-093-mathbbr-2k-is-theoretically-la.evolution: The representatives extend from vector-space indexing and sparse embeddings to learned hashing and dynamic indexing. Recent work examines theoretical embedding requirements for top-k retrieval, sparse multi-vector representations, and uncertainty-aware cross-modal hashing designed to reduce the effect of unreliable labels.
openQuestions: Which geometric properties best predict retrieval failures after compression?
How should retrieval systems express uncertainty when semantic similarity and label supervision disagree?
topic-093-mathbbr-2k-is-theoretically-la.overview: Similarity search retrieves nearby or relevant items without exhaustively comparing every candidate. This topic includes approximate nearest-neighbor algorithms, compact binary hashes, learned indexes, and multi-vector retrieval. A representative hashing method learns binary codes whose Hamming distances reconstruct distances in the original space, explicitly linking compression to the relationships that search should preserve.
topic-093-mathbbr-2k-is-theoretically-la.title: Similarity Search, Learned Hashing, and Retrieval Geometry
topic-093-mathbbr-2k-is-theoretically-la.whyItMatters: Large collections require a balance between retrieval quality, memory, and latency. Learned representations can improve that balance, but noisy labels or mismatched similarity notions may make efficient search consistently retrieve the wrong items.

topic-094-textit-trans-lora-towards-data.evolution: The representatives include early adapters and structured compression, followed by layer sampling and projected-gradient training. Recent papers analyze differences from full fine-tuning, improve low-rank update scaling, and allocate compression ranks according to estimated loss sensitivity across a model.
openQuestions: How can a training procedure identify which layers and ranks a new task needs?
When do memory savings translate into lower end-to-end time and energy?
topic-094-textit-trans-lora-towards-data.overview: Large models can be expensive to adapt because training stores gradients and optimizer state as well as parameters. This topic explores low-rank updates, gradient projection, selective layer training, and low-rank compression. These methods save different resources: some restrict trainable directions, while others change which layers or singular components receive computation.
topic-094-textit-trans-lora-towards-data.title: Low-Rank Adaptation and Memory-Efficient Model Training
topic-094-textit-trans-lora-towards-data.whyItMatters: Efficiency claims need to be assessed alongside the expressive capacity retained by the update. A small adaptation budget may work well for one task but prevent changes required by another, making rank allocation and parameter selection substantive modeling decisions.

topic-095-g-2-reader-dual-evolving-graph.evolution: Earlier representatives concern information retrieval and query learning. Later work combines dense retrieval with sequence generation. Recent studies emphasize realistic corpora, multi-system routing, temporal knowledge, and detecting or repairing retrieval failures before downstream answers are produced.
openQuestions: How can systems distinguish missing evidence from a failure to retrieve existing evidence?
What evaluations measure end-to-end faithfulness across changing, heterogeneous knowledge collections?
topic-095-g-2-reader-dual-evolving-graph.overview: Retrieval-augmented generation combines a language model with an external collection of information. The retriever selects evidence that the generator can use, making knowledge access a separate component from what is stored in model parameters. This cluster studies retrieval chains, routing, technical-document evaluation, large data lakes, and gaps in what retrievers can find.
topic-095-g-2-reader-dual-evolving-graph.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Knowledge Access
topic-095-g-2-reader-dual-evolving-graph.whyItMatters: External evidence can improve specificity and support updating knowledge, but generation remains limited by retrieval quality. Relevant entities may be poorly positioned in an embedding space, leaving blind spots even when the required information exists in the collection.
